mcqs.learning_point: Understand the purpose of local self-government
mcqs.question: Consider a village where the local council decides to build a community well, repairs a school, and organizes a health camp after consulting the villagers. What is the primary purpose of such local self‑government (Panchayati Raj) as illustrated by this example?

options.A: To enable villagers to directly participate in planning and implementing development activities in their community.
options.B: To replace the state government in all administrative functions.
options.C: To collect taxes for the central government.
options.D: To ensure that only elected officials make decisions without community input.

mcqs.answer: To enable villagers to directly participate in planning and implementing development activities in their community.
mcqs.explanation: Local self‑government is intended to bring decision‑making to the grassroots, allowing villagers to identify their needs and take part in development projects. Options B, C and D describe functions that are not the core purpose of Panchayati Raj.

mcqs.question: In a village, all adult residents gather in the open ground every month to discuss the need for a new irrigation canal, approve the village budget, and elect members of the local council. Which body is described in this scenario?
mcqs.explanation: The Gram Sabha is a meeting of all adult villagers that deliberates on development plans, budgets and elects representatives. The Gram Panchayat is the elected executive body, not the gathering of all villagers. Options B and D refer to higher‑level administrative offices.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the Gram Panchayat is a common misconception?

options.A: The Gram Panchayat consists of elected representatives, not all villagers, and makes decisions on their behalf.
options.B: The Gram Panchayat meets only once a year.
options.C: The Gram Panchayat has authority to enact national laws.
options.D: The Gram Panchayat is appointed by the state government.

mcqs.answer: The Gram Panchayat consists of elected representatives, not all villagers, and makes decisions on their behalf.
mcqs.explanation: Many think the Gram Panchayat includes every adult villager, but it is a body of elected members who represent the community. Options B, C and D are also incorrect statements, but the question asks for the common misconception, which is that it includes all villagers.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise the role of elected representatives
mcqs.question: Elected members of the Gram Panchayat are expected to:

options.A: Formulate village development plans based on the needs expressed in the Gram Sabha.
options.B: Unilaterally allocate funds without consulting villagers.
options.C: Supervise only the collection of taxes, not development activities.
options.D: Represent the village only in state‑level meetings, not in local matters.

mcqs.answer: Formulate village development plans based on the needs expressed in the Gram Sabha.
mcqs.explanation: The core role of elected representatives is to translate the aspirations voiced in the Gram Sabha into concrete development plans. Options B, C and D describe actions that contradict the participatory nature of Panchayati Raj.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand basic functions of rural local bodies
mcqs.question: Which pair correctly matches the level of rural local body with one of its primary functions?

options.A: Gram Panchayat – implementation of government schemes at the village level.
options.B: Block Panchayat – conducting village‑level Gram Sabha meetings.
options.D: Block Panchayat – issuing birth and death certificates for individual households.

mcqs.answer: Gram Panchayat – implementation of government schemes at the village level.
mcqs.explanation: Gram Panchayats are responsible for executing development schemes and welfare programmes within the village. Block Panchayats coordinate activities among several Gram Panchayats and do not conduct Gram Sabha meetings (B) nor issue individual certificates (D). Supervising district hospitals (C) is a function of higher‑level health administration.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise citizen participation in village governance
mcqs.question: All of the following are ways in which citizens can actively participate in village governance EXCEPT:

options.A: Attending Gram Sabha meetings and voicing opinions.
options.B: Voting in elections for Panchayat members.
options.C: Submitting written suggestions to the Gram Panchayat.
options.D: Appointing the Sarpanch without an election.

mcqs.answer: Appointing the Sarpanch without an election.
mcqs.explanation: Citizen participation includes attending meetings, voting, and providing feedback. The Sarpanch (village head) is elected; appointing them without an election bypasses democratic participation, making option D the correct exception.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the purpose of local self-government
mcqs.question: The main purpose of local self‑government (Panchayati Raj) in rural India is to:

options.A: Allow villagers to manage their own affairs and development.
options.B: Centralize power in the state capital.

mcqs.answer: Allow villagers to manage their own affairs and development.
mcqs.explanation: Panchayati Raj devolves authority to the grassroots so that people can decide on local issues. Options B, C and D describe functions that are outside the scope of local self‑government.

mcqs.question: The Gram Sabha in a village is best described as:

options.A: A meeting of all adult residents of the village to discuss and approve local matters.
options.B: The office of the district collector.
options.C: A committee of only the elected Panchayat members.

mcqs.answer: A meeting of all adult residents of the village to discuss and approve local matters.
mcqs.explanation: Gram Sabha is the assembly of all adult villagers, serving as the supreme decision‑making body at the village level. The other options refer to different administrative entities.
